comment: A really tough teacher to work with. if you want an A you need to study maybe 25 hours a week for this class. he barely does practice problems and that's only in class. he doesn't give a study guide and is very reliant on test grades.

DO NOT take this guy for corporate finance. Top 3 worst professors I've had at UR. Extremely lazy, does not care to help students or learn their names. Your entire grade depends on a couple of tests that he does not prepare you for. No study guides for tests and he does't care to help his students. If you want to maintain your GPA do not take him.
Definitely a hard class and there are virtually no resources to study for a test. I would quite litterly would rather my pet Ferrit teach the class.

David North is the worst professor I have at UR. He provides 0 material on the tests other than the slides he does in class, and his lecture slides are useless for studying, consisting of poorly worded problems with no answer key. It is mind blowing that he believes this is the best way to educate his students. His lack of care is disturbing.

Knows a lot and the class is really interesting if you're into valuations. He won't help you out with assignments because he wants you to figure it out yourself, but he goes through every assignment in class so ask him when he's presenting. 2 exams and +10 assignments. If you had him for corporate finance, Cases should be relatively easy.

Doesn't make a huge effort to teach. He refuses any questions asked about assignments. He mostly wants students to figure stuff out on their own while including a textbook in the syllabus that he doesn't teach out of. He is also overall very rude.

Dr. North is extremely knowledgeable on all things finance and is a really smart professor. However, hes one of the worst communicators outside of class and never wants to help the student at all. Classes are pretty boring and the tests are hard, but the assignments are very doable. I suggest taking someone different who could help more.

Dr. North is super intelligent on all things finance, but could care less about helping students outside of class. The material is very challenging for those not gifted in finance and he makes you feel bad for trying to meet with him. Also don't try emailing him because at best you will get back a one word reply. The class is doable but a struggle.
Curves a lot of his tests. Can be boring at times but it's corporate finance so what do you expect. Super nice and reasonable with partial credit

Dr North is the best professor I had at UR hands down. Cases & Financial Modeling is a must take in the finance department, especially if you want to do corporate finance. Assignments and projects are applicable and very useful to learn how to model this stuff in excel. Super nice guy as well. Just put some effort in, don't take for an easy A.

His class is very boring and useless. He reads through the slides quickly and expects you to know everything. Although this is a high level finance class, he's unwilling to help students. He grades homework in a random way. Basically, the grades are based on his mood I would say. I don't want to pay such a high tuition for a professor like him.

Going to class is utterly useless... He goes through the slide shows on an overhead and circles stuff.  You will have to teach yourself everything.  The tests are extremely hard and he will do everything in his power to avoid helping you if you go to his office hours.  He assigns models almost every class but never explains how to do them.
Dr. North is awesome. He also curves hard.

North is a great guy.  The amount of work required outside class is pertty minimal and managable and every class is a lecture.  If you like finance, this will be a good class for you.  Hard not to get and A or a B after he scales.

Definitely not an easy A, but possible.  He gives a midterm and a final, but it's not cumulative.  We have weekly quizzes and models roughly every other week.  He's a pretty fair professor and so is his class.
